messages.subject: Quick question -- I hope
parts:
All,

I’m attempting to do an efa in lavaan. I installed the latest developmental version and verified this using sessionInfo(“lavaan”) which came back with other attached packages:
[1] lavaan_0.6-13.1798

However, when I attempt to run efa.model.3factor.fit <- efa(data = MGMT9610r[,time1.var.names], nfactors = 1:3), I get the following error: Error in efa(data = MGMT9610r[, time1.var.names], nfactors = 1:3) :
could not find function “efa"

When I simply do the default install of lavann without the developmental install, it states that package 6.12 is installed. Any suggestions would be greatly appreciated.

Many thanks — Bob Vandenberg

messages.author: b40b733c4b3d58f4
messages.subject: Re: Quick question -- I hope
parts:
All,

Never mind about the question below. I figured that one out — user error as usual. But I do have one remaining question. Namely, it appears that the default version of lavaan at CRAN is 0.6-12. Yet in the tutorial at lavaan.ugent.be, the efa example (also the ESEM examples) use a version of 6.13. This is confusing to me. Can I use the efa function with version 6.12 or do I need to download the latest developmental version of the 6.13?

Thanks in advance for your assistance.

Bob Vandenberg

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Quick question -- I hope
parts:
On 12/23/22 18:53, Bob Vandenberg wrote:
> However, when I attempt to run efa.model.3factor.fit <- efa(data =
> MGMT9610r[,time1.var.names], nfactors = 1:3), I get the following
> error: Error in efa(data = MGMT9610r[, time1.var.names], nfactors =
> 1:3) : could not find function “efa"

Hm. What happens if you use lavaan:::efa() instead?

It should work. And you should be able to see the man page by typing

?efa

at the prompt.

Are you using RStudio? If so, try again using the standard R program
outside RStudio.

Yves.

The documentation anticipates the release of 0.6-13 (in a few weeks, I
hope). To be clear: efa() is not available in 0.6-12.

Yves.
